codeReview.summary: The sidepanel portion of VAL-CRIT-003 is implemented correctly: runtime and storage listeners are stored and removed via SidePanelUI.destroy() on pagehide/beforeunload. However, the content-script portion is incomplete because ContentScriptHandler.destroy() is never wired to any lifecycle event or external caller, so the content.ts runtime listener still leaks for the lifetime of the page.

issues.description: The new destroy() method is unreachable in production: the file only instantiates `new ContentScriptHandler()` and never stores the instance, registers `destroy()` on `pagehide/beforeunload`, or exposes any cleanup hook. As a result, `chrome.runtime.onMessage.removeListener(this.messageListener)` is never called, so the content-script runtime listener leak described by VAL-CRIT-003 remains unfixed.

destroy() clears UI state with `clearActionOverlay()` and `clearBadge()`, which only hide DOM elements rather than removing them. This does not block VAL-CRIT-003, but it means the content-script cleanup path would still leave overlay/badge DOM nodes allocated if destroy() were ever invoked.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The cleanup-worker skill says memory leak fixes must 'Ensure cleanup is called', but the worker marked the feature complete after adding an uninvoked destroy() in content.ts. The skill procedure is correct; the transcript shows the worker did not validate that the content-script cleanup path was actually reachable.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Skill: .factory/skills/cleanup-worker/SKILL.md section 'Fix Memory Leaks' step 4. Transcript/handoff claim destroy() was added in content.ts, but code shows only `new ContentScriptHandler();` at packages/extension/content.ts:100 and no pagehide/unload hook or exported cleanup handle anywhere in the extension.

summary: Fail. Sidepanel listener cleanup is wired correctly, but the content-script listener cleanup is dead code because ContentScriptHandler.destroy() is never called. Blocking issue: packages/extension/content.ts still leaks its runtime onMessage listener for the life of the page.
